sentences.text: The Geminids are the richest meteor shower of the year: at peak, under a dark sky, up to one hundred fifty meteors an hour.
Their source is not a comet but the asteroid 3200 Phaethon, which comes closer to the Sun than Mercury; the Sun's heat cracks its surface and scatters dust.
Every December Earth passes through the dust trail stretched along Phaethon's orbit; the particles enter the atmosphere at thirty-five kilometres a second and often leave colourful, slow trails.
The meteors seem to spray from one point in the sky, the radiant in the constellation Gemini: this is the direction in which Earth is cutting through the stream.
The best time to watch is after midnight; this year the Moon is a thin crescent, sets early, and the sky stays dark.
